entries.title: Arrest without warrant and notice of appearance
entries.analysis: The arrest and appearance-notice rules are consolidated. Subsection (7) introduces an additional prior-permission safeguard for specified persons and offences.

entries.title: Arrest procedure and officer duties
entries.analysis: Review identification, arrest memorandum and notification duties under the revised provision.

entries.title: Access to advocate during interrogation
entries.analysis: The right to meet an advocate during interrogation remains subject to the statutory scope.

entries.title: Communication of arrest grounds and bail rights
entries.analysis: Check communication of grounds and information about bail where applicable.

entries.title: Informing relatives or friends of arrest
entries.analysis: The revised framework also refers to the designated police officer in the district.

entries.title: Maintenance of wives, children and parents
entries.analysis: The corresponding maintenance remedy is subject to the statutory eligibility conditions and applicable procedural law.

entries.title: Urgent orders concerning nuisance or apprehended danger
entries.analysis: The emergency preventive power is relocated; examine its statutory conditions and duration.

entries.title: Land or water disputes and breach of peace
entries.analysis: This preventive procedure does not itself conclusively determine civil title.

entries.title: Compliance with lawful police directions
entries.analysis: A separately numbered provision imposes obligations concerning lawful directions under the relevant chapter. Its scope is statutory, not a general unrestricted police power.

entries.title: First information report (FIR)
entries.analysis: The revised provision expressly addresses territorial flexibility and electronic reporting, and permits a conditional preliminary inquiry for a specified class of offences.

entries.title: Non-cognizable information and investigation
entries.analysis: The provision includes additional reporting requirements to the Magistrate.

entries.title: Investigation of cognizable cases and Magistrate directions
entries.analysis: Magistrate-directed investigation has additional procedural requirements. Examine subsections (3) and (4) separately.

entries.title: Investigation procedure and forensic examination
entries.analysis: Subsection (3) introduces forensic crime-scene requirements for offences meeting the punishment threshold, subject to the prescribed notification framework.

entries.title: Police examination of witnesses
entries.analysis: Compare the rules governing oral examination and recording of statements.

entries.title: Police statements and their use
entries.analysis: The restrictions on use of police statements remain important; consult the evidentiary exceptions.

entries.title: Magistrate recording of confessions and statements
entries.analysis: The revised provision includes additional requirements for recording particular witness statements and electronic recording.

entries.title: Remand and default bail
entries.analysis: The framework allows the aggregate fifteen days of police custody to be authorised in parts within the specified initial forty- or sixty-day window. Check the separate detention limits in subsection (3).

entries.title: Police report on completion of investigation
entries.analysis: The new text includes electronic reporting and progress communication to the informant or victim; further investigation during trial has a separate proviso.

entries.title: Cognizance by Magistrates
entries.analysis: Determine the appropriate route for cognizance and any preconditions in the relevant provisions.

entries.title: Examination of complainant
entries.analysis: The revised text adds a pre-cognizance hearing proviso and special provisions for complaints against public servants. Check controlling judicial interpretation and special-law exceptions.

entries.title: Supply of police report and documents
entries.analysis: The new provision specifies a fourteen-day outer period from production or appearance of the accused and addresses supply to represented victims and electronic copies.

entries.title: Compounding of offences
entries.analysis: Use the relevant statutory tables, permissions and conditions; not every offence may be compounded.

entries.title: Bail in bailable offences
entries.analysis: Check the applicable bond or bail-bond requirements.

entries.title: Maximum undertrial detention
entries.analysis: The revised provision adds a one-third threshold for qualifying first-time offenders and restrictions relating to multiple cases, alongside other statutory exceptions.

entries.title: Bail in non-bailable offences
entries.analysis: The revised text changes certain provisos. Examine statutory exceptions and the court's discretion.

entries.title: Anticipatory bail
entries.analysis: The corresponding pre-arrest bail remedy remains subject to the statutory conditions and exclusions. Compare the actual text, including the excluded offences.

entries.title: High Court and Sessions Court bail powers
entries.analysis: The special bail powers are relocated; examine conditions and applicable special statutes.

entries.title: Witness protection scheme
entries.analysis: A separate provision requires a state witness-protection scheme; verify the relevant notified scheme.

entries.title: Inherent powers of High Court
entries.analysis: The saving of inherent High Court powers is relocated; quashing remains subject to judicial principles and the facts.

entries.title: Repeal and savings
entries.analysis: BNSS saves specified pending appeals, applications, trials, inquiries and investigations immediately before commencement. Do not determine applicability solely by the new section number.
